purpose.summary: Join the existing upstream public synthetic plugin engine to the actual bounded local-regtest daemon service, with explicit default-OFF admission and process-reopen HTTP witnesses.
scope: Direct parent is the accepted public PR55 head; no unrelated source or incoming private artifact.
Separate default-OFF build and runtime opt-ins; exact existing public synthetic plugin only, no arbitrary path, class, mode or operator configuration.
Own upstream PluginContext on the joined startup thread until worker, HTTP and database users have stopped; keep Python and index work outside native locks.
Bind fixed exact source/config/Python identity before import and refuse incompatible index roots without wipe, identity rewrite or automatic repair.
Observe parent/child ALP metadata, groups, history and UTXOs through the existing upstream router across pending/confirmed process reopen and native reorg.
Retain every inherited component selection, assertion,60-second deadline, default-OFF smoke and cleanup predicate; add a separate fifth integration profile.
exclusions: No new plugin engine, token algorithm, consensus, native validation/mempool policy, network parameter, dependency or activation change.
No arbitrary/operator/private plugin, Python sandbox claim, public exposure, WebSocket/broadcast, unbounded history, DB wipe or migration authority.
No private history, incoming evidence, operator data, server access, deployment, cutover, release, desktop integration or automatic proof promotion.

expected_results: Exact native owner case12 assertions per repetition,18 fresh daemons, runtime plugin-OFF absence, non-plugin-index refusal, pending/confirmed restart and reorg parity, config-drift refusal and continued native mining. Join and disposable cleanup precede exclusive normalized report creation.

Concurrent old-transaction reads are either canonical 200 or protobuf 503, never a fabricated or partial response. After file removal the old transaction is 503; a retained recent transaction remains 200 and the node continues at its accepted height.

scenarios.command: Existing observer profile only, retained by chronik-port-core.yml: Run feature_chronik_token_http.py: extend to height 290 in bounded batches, disconnect below the retained projection anchor, reconsider, verify mismatched restart leaves HTTP disabled, then explicitly full-reindex. Separately exercise upstream retained-anchor and source-generation contradictions; the fixture observer closes while native progress continues.
expected_results: Inherited observer coverage only; this scenario does not establish the upstream daemon's readiness.
Both known and unknown token/transaction IDs return protobuf 503 after observer closure, never stale 200 or misleading 404.

Node RPC and chain selection continue; reconsider does not reopen observation. A persistent-tip mismatch disables HTTP on restart and logs recovery=reindex. Explicit full reindex restores canonical token metadata and byte-identical confirmed transaction output.
failure_conditions: Any accepted response after irreversible closure, missing-ID 404 from a degraded view, HTTP serving from a mismatched restarted runtime, missing mismatch diagnostic, failed canonical reindex recovery, node-authority effect, skip, timeout or nonzero exit.

limitations: Bounded unpruned local regtest only. Existing graph/pool/payload/callback limits are not RSS, latency, full-chain availability or power-loss durability claims.

Exact trusted public synthetic plugin only. Python is not sandboxed. Operator plugins, actual-daemon incompatible-version tests and the full ALP cycle with plugins remain later separate scopes; existing component/process version and exception witnesses remain required.
No operator database migration contract. Different adapter or plugin identities refuse existing indexes without wipe or rewrite.
All native values and fees are zero; synthetic priority deltas are not actual currency. ALP quantities test upstream interpretation, not funded economics.
No incoming reports or independent public reproduction. Rust registry inputs are locked; OS/SDK/runner inputs are not. Upstream dependency alerts and historical timeout counterevidence remain open.
counterevidence: Immutable changes0049-0052 retain earlier60-second matrix refusals. Later PR55 Linux and local successes do not establish every prior failure cause or remove counterevidence.

The initial local normal combined-profile ten-repetition component matrix refused runtime-stop-and-reopen-controls at repetition 3 under the unchanged 60-second process limit. The first three groups passed ten repetitions each, but that run produced no complete passing component report.

Local preflight of the new actual-daemon plugin client passed three repetitions/18 daemons plus the runtime-OFF smoke. These are separate bounded observations, not incoming public evidence, independent reproduction or a substitute for the refused full matrix.

The 60-second bound covers the complete 13-case selected process, not one case. Private instrumented samples continued through multiple cases and sampled upstream database synchronization during reopen. They remain non-qualifying and do not establish every uninstrumented timeout cause or a plugin deadlock.

The service and plugin profiles previously rejected their combination. Removing that guard alone would not own the context through joined teardown or bind plugin identity; this change explicitly supplies those owners and checks.
Component plugin success does not establish actual daemon behavior. New real-process checks must independently pass before PR preparation; metadata alone is not an observed execution.
